discrepancies.why: The building is leased to one operator, so occupancy of the lease itself is 100% and income is that operator's covenant. Behind the lease the operator sub-lets 84 of 96 units (87.5%) and collects about AED 5,440,500 a year against the AED 6,257,000 it pays, while bearing the running costs: the rent is supported by the operator, not earned by the units. That is covenant risk. At expiry, or if the operator fails, income falls to what the sub-tenancies earn. Whether the operator is related to the seller is a separate question, decided only on stated evidence. Review: The OM states the master tenant (Oryx Lane Property Management L.L.C) and the Seller are under common ownership, so the rent is an intra-group payment, not arm's-length third-party income. The lease is fixed with no escalation and expires 31 March 2028. The headline rent and yield rest on the operator's covenant and on a related party's willingness to keep paying. Sub-tenants pay less than the master rent, and the operator carries the shortfall. After expiry the buyer is exposed to the underlying sub-tenant rents, a softer market and 12 vacant units.

impact.basis: master-lease rent above what the sub-tenancies pay

discrepancies.analyst_action: Obtain the master lease, the operator's accounts and ownership, and the seller's ownership; confirm in writing whether the operator is related to the seller.
discrepancies.related_party_note: the review found a likely connection, but no verified quote states that the operator and the seller are related; left unknown for the analyst

discrepancies.title: OM calls AED 6,257,000 'passing rent from the current rent roll' but its own rent-roll tables are on lower sub-tenant rent

sources.quote: Passing rent from the current rent roll is AED 6,257,000 per annum.
sources.label: verified quote

discrepancies.why: The OM describes the master-lease rent as the rent roll figure. Its own floor-by-floor and expiry tables, labelled as coming from the rent roll, sum to about AED 5.44m, the same as the code-parsed sub-tenant rent. The 'share' percentages in the tenant and expiry tables are also computed on that lower base. The headline rent and 8.40% yield therefore describe an operator payment, not rent collected from occupiers.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the broker to reconcile the AED 6,257,000 headline to the sub-tenancy schedule and the Ejari register. Re-base the yield on sub-tenant rent (AED 5.44m) as well as on master rent.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 8.4% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 4,633,382 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 7.9%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

discrepancies.why: The operating costs quoted come from a landlord-level statement. The master tenant bears leasing, FM, cleaning, security and common-area utilities, and those costs are not shown. The statement also has no vacancy or collection-loss lines. Any net income or yield built on these costs is overstated once the master lease ends or if the buyer takes over operations.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Request the operator's own P&L and budget for FM, leasing, utilities and security. Build a stabilised operating cost line for direct management and apply it to sub-tenant rent.

discrepancies.why: The OM's unit mix lists only studios, 1-bedroom and 2-bedroom apartments totalling 96 units, yet it mentions shops. This is an unexplained inconsistency in what the building contains and what income and VAT treatment applies.

notices.text: Cheque profile: 34% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 41% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 25% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Master lease, operator accounts and ownership, and the novation terms of the sub-tenancies at expiry.

disc.master_lease_related_party.title.label: discrepancy: master lease

disc.master_lease_related_party.why.value: The building is leased to one operator, so occupancy of the lease itself is 100% and income is that operator's covenant. Behind the lease the operator sub-lets 84 of 96 units (87.5%) and collects about AED 5,440,500 a year against the AED 6,257,000 it pays, while bearing the running costs: the rent is supported by the operator, not earned by the units. That is covenant risk. At expiry, or if the operator fails, income falls to what the sub-tenancies earn. Whether the operator is related to the seller is a separate question, decided only on stated evidence. Review: The OM states the master tenant (Oryx Lane Property Management L.L.C) and the Seller are under common ownership, so the rent is an intra-group payment, not arm's-length third-party income. The lease is fixed with no escalation and expires 31 March 2028. The headline rent and yield rest on the operator's covenant and on a related party's willingness to keep paying. Sub-tenants pay less than the master rent, and the operator carries the shortfall. After expiry the buyer is exposed to the underlying sub-tenant rents, a softer market and 12 vacant units.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the deal is blocked on whether the master tenant is related to the seller, which the documents do not state. Nothing else matters until that is confirmed in writing.

Separately, the screen shows returns well short of the mandate on the firm's house view (screen reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Oryx Lane Residences, Dubai Silicon Oasis, 96 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2019 [[deal.completion_year]].
- **Price:** asking AED 74.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], AED 1,007 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] on net sellable area.
- **Income:** the whole building is leased to one operator, Oryx Lane Property Management L.L.C, at AED 6.3m [[rr.master_lease_rent_aed]] a year. The lease expires 31 March 2028 [[rr.master_lease_end]]. Behind it, the operator sub-lets 84 [[rr.let_units]] units at AED 5.4m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] in-place rent, which is 88% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy. The screen underwrites 100% [[uw.occupancy_by_units]] because the master lease pays on every unit.

## Returns
Unlevered, pre-tax:

| Measure | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR | a loss of 1.7% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple | 0.93x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 7.6% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.8% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 7.1% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |

Year-1 NOI is AED 5.6m [[uw.noi_year1]]. The yield test passes. The IRR and multiple tests fail.

Levered returns, secondary: a loss of 9.0% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] a year and an equity multiple of 0.64x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]]. Year-1 DSCR is 1.55x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM's headline yield is 8.4% [[om.yield_stated]], gross on asking price. On the buyer's basis, Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs, it is 7.1% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. That is 1.3 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] lower.

## What would make it fail
- **Returns miss in every sensitivity case.** The best case has market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter. Unlevered IRR there is 0.8% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], far under the target. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, it is a loss of 4.1% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **The master lease ends inside the hold.** After expiry, income falls to what the sub-tenancies earn. The master rent exceeds sub-tenant rent by AED 816k [[disc.master_lease_related_party.impact_aed]] a year. The screen's forward NOI is AED 4.1m [[uw.forward_noi_aed]], and the gross exit value is AED 52.9m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], well below asking.
- **Costs are thin.** The operating statement omits maintenance, common utilities, and security and cleaning. The screen filled these from mandate defaults. The chiller arrangement is unstated, so district cooling is also a default, at AED 666k [[uw.opex_default.district_cooling]].

## Discrepancies
Lower-severity items are not discussed here.

1. **Master lease, possibly to a related party (high).** The documents show a fixed-rent lease to one operator with no escalation. The operator pays AED 6.3m [[rr.master_lease_rent_aed]] against about AED 5.4m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] collected from sub-tenants, and carries the running costs. The title puts the master rent 15.0% [[disc.master_lease_related_party.title]] over the sub-tenants' rent. The review notes the OM describes common ownership of operator and seller. The screen treats the relationship as unconfirmed. It relied on master rent to expiry, then on sub-tenancies novating to the owner. The impact is AED 816k [[disc.master_lease_related_party.impact_aed]] of income that rests on the operator's covenant, not on the units.
2. **OM yield before acquisition costs (medium).** The OM's 8.4% [[om.yield_stated]] is on asking price, before acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]]. The same income on price plus costs gives 7.9% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]], 0.5 points [[disc.yield_excludes_acquisition_costs.impact_ratio]] lower. The screen uses yield on total cost.

## Checks before diligence
- **Blocking:** written confirmation from the seller on whether the operator is related to it.
- Obtain the master lease, the operator's accounts and ownership, and the seller's ownership.
- Ask the broker to restate the yield on total cost.
- Confirm from the title deed, completion certificate and rent roll whether any ground-floor shops exist and how they are let.
- Verify the OM figures that failed verification: operating costs, chiller arrangement and lease structure.
- Notice on cheque profile: 34% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on one or two cheques, and 25% [[notice.cheque_profile]] is on six or more. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.
- Master lease documents, including novation terms at expiry.

## Assumptions
The exit yield is 7.8% [[uw.exit_yield]], which includes 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion plus an age premium. The hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. Market rent falls 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2. It then rises 2% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss is 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. The loan is AED 33.5m [[uw.loan_aed]] at 45% [[uw.ltv]] LTV. It is sized at 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] cover, with 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] interest and 15 years [[assume.amortisation_years]] of amortisation. District cooling, common utilities, maintenance, security and cleaning, and marketing and leasing are mandate defaults because the package lacked them.
